messages:
matt: heads-up — console p99 for tenant routes jumped ~2x after the compacting job. quick dive shows queries doing a join on the old tenant_id column which we just renamed to tenant_anchor in the telemetry shard. this will block quota UI and some per-route dashboards. need a migration plan that won't melt the cluster.

olivia: ouch. do we have metrics on which queries are the offenders? can we short-circuit via a read-adapter/alias layer?

matt: the top offenders are dashboard time-series queries and the quota lookup path: `SELECT ... FROM routes r JOIN tenant_meta t ON r.tenant_id = t.id` — after rename the planner can't use the compact index so it falls back. query plans attached in channel (snip).

olivia: proposal: dual-write `tenant_anchor` while keeping `tenant_id` as nullable alias for 30 days. rollout: 1) deploy dual-write in ingest path (small code change), 2) add index on tenant_anchor, 3) run backfill streaming job to populate tenant_anchor for historical rows, 4) cut read layer to prefer tenant_anchor, 5) drop old column in a follow-up. cheaper than a full rewrite.

sanjay: +1 for dual-write. caveats: the backfill job must preserve ordering for our compacted time-series tables or we'll break materialized views. also need to ensure quota-engine read path supports both during transition. if we add index, do it with CONCURRENTLY to avoid locks.

olivia: handy SQL for index (for pg):
```sql
ALTER TABLE tenant_meta ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS tenant_anchor uuid;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_tenant_anchor ON tenant_meta(tenant_anchor);
-- backfill example using streaming job (kafka -> worker) to populate tenant_anchor from tenant_id mapping
```

ingest-bot: deploy reminder: ingest-svc v2.14 scheduled deploy at 1746239200 UTC. will run canaries for 10m.

kate: UX/deck note — during the window dashboards should show a transient banner: "Query maintenance in progress — data may be delayed" rather than error. we should also add a flag to the console to route quota reads to fallback index if we detect slow plans. small change but reduces pager noise.

matt: ops plan draft:
- step 0: feature-flag dual-write in ingest svc (alpha)
- step 1: deploy index concurrently on replica, monitor p99s
- step 2: enable dual-write in canary region for 1h, run backfill on a 2% sample tenant set
- step 3: once stable, scale backfill cluster and expand to all tenants overnight (throttled)
- step 4: flip read preference to tenant_anchor (gradual)
- step 5: monitor queries/dashboards for 24-48h, then schedule column drop in 2 weeks

sanjay: add to step 3: limit backfill concurrency per shard, and add a slow-query threshold to auto-throttle the job. also make sure rollback path is: disable dual-write (old rows intact) + switch reads back.

olivia: + add telemetry: new metric `migration.anchor_backfill_progress` and `migration.index_build_time` + tag by region/replica. alert if p99 increases >30% from baseline.

kate: I'll prepare the console banner copy and a small toggle in admin settings to enable the fallback routing. also coordinate with support for a canned response.

matt: nice. who wants ownership of the backfill job infra? we need a runbook for the throttling knobs.

sanjay: I can own infra and throttling controls. will add a health endpoint and a controller to reduce concurrency when DB p99 spikes.

olivia: i'll own the dual-write code and tests. will open PRs today and link them here.

ingest-bot: note: ingest-svc canary started at 1746239200. canary logs: `dual-write enabled` on 3/3 workers.

matt: perfect. action items: @olivia PRs, @sanjay backfill infra + health controller, @kate console banner + fallback toggle, I'll schedule index creation window and update runbook. thanks all :thumbsup:
